overview:
Juan Vargas, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by eleven points on the partisan vote index. He advanced to the general election and faces Republican Jeff Belle, a challenger with minimal financial backing. Vargas has raised about $568,000 and holds roughly $164,000 on hand, while Belle has raised about $25,000 with under $1,400 remaining. Little outside money is engaged on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets price a Vargas win at roughly 96 percent. The combination of a favorable district, incumbent strength, and a heavily outspent opponent makes this seat solidly Democratic, with little evidence suggesting a competitive contest.
